product.name: Tool Share
product.problem: Tool requests are scattered across a neighbourhood chat group, nobody knows who has which tool, and lent tools go missing.
targetUsers: Neighbourhood members who lend and borrow tools
A volunteer organiser who invites members
product.valueProposition: Find a tool nearby in seconds and always know where lent tools are.
mvpScope: Member sign-up and sign-in with an invitation code
List a tool with a description and availability
Browse and search the neighbourhood catalogue
Lender approves or declines, and marks the tool returned
My loans: what I borrowed and lent
product.differentiation: Built for one closed community: invitation-only, no marketplace features, no payments, minimal personal data.
product.businessModel: Free for members; hosting kept under 10 USD per month. A donation link may be added later.

functional.title: Member accounts
functional.description: A person with a valid invitation code signs up with name, email and password; members sign in and out.
acceptanceCriteria: Sign-up without a valid invitation code is refused
A member can sign in and sign out
Passwords are never stored in plain text

functional.title: List a tool
functional.description: A member lists a tool with name, description, category and whether it is available; they can edit or withdraw it.
acceptanceCriteria: A listed tool appears in the catalogue
Only the owner can edit or withdraw a tool

functional.title: Browse and search
functional.description: Members browse available tools and search by name or category.
acceptanceCriteria: Search by a word in the name returns matching tools
Filtering by category works
Withdrawn tools are not shown

functional.title: Request a loan
functional.description: A member requests a tool for a start and end date.
acceptanceCriteria: A request needs a start date not in the past and an end date after it
A member cannot request their own tool
Overlapping approved loans are refused

functional.title: Approve, decline and return
functional.description: The lender approves or declines a request and marks an approved loan as returned.
acceptanceCriteria: Only the lender can approve, decline or mark returned
A returned tool becomes available again

functional.title: My loans
functional.description: Members see what they borrowed and lent, with overdue loans highlighted.
acceptanceCriteria: Borrowed and lent loans are listed separately
Loans past their end date and not returned are marked overdue

functional.title: Email reminders
acceptanceCriteria: A reminder is sent the day after the end date

nonFunctional.requirement: Passwords hashed with scrypt; session cookies are HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax and Secure in production; state-changing forms are protected against CSRF.
Pages meet WCAG 2.1 AA for contrast, labels and keyboard use.
Every page works on a 360 px wide phone without horizontal scrolling.
Only name, email and password hash are stored about a member; emails are not shown to other members.

userStories.soThat: I do not have to buy one
acceptanceCriteria: I can search for 'ladder' and request one for Saturday

userStories.iWant: to see who has my drill
acceptanceCriteria: My lent loans show the borrower's name and end date
Sign-up requires the invitation code

stack.rationale: One language for server and tests; the factory already validates with Node.
stack.tradeoffs: Single-threaded; fine for a neighbourhood-sized app.

stack.choice: Node's built-in http module with a small router
stack.rationale: No framework dependency to learn or update; pages are simple forms.
stack.tradeoffs: More code for routing and forms than a framework would need.

stack.rationale: Fast on phones, accessible by default, no build step for a client framework.
stack.tradeoffs: Less interactive than a single-page app.

stack.choice: SQLite through Node's built-in node:sqlite module
stack.rationale: A single file, no separate database server, no monthly cost.
stack.tradeoffs: One writer at a time; moving to Postgres would need a data migration.

architecture.frontend: Server-rendered HTML pages with semantic forms and one shared stylesheet; no client-side framework.
architecture.backend: A Node.js HTTP server with modules for routing, sessions, members, tools and loans; all input validated on the server.
architecture.database: SQLite file at DATABASE_PATH with tables member, tool and loan; schema created and upgraded by numbered migration scripts.

integrations.name: Email delivery (post-MVP)
integrations.purpose: Overdue reminders (FR-7), not part of the MVP.

architecture.authentication: Email and password with scrypt hashing; sign-up requires the invitation code from INVITE_CODE; server-side sessions in SQLite referenced by a signed cookie.
architecture.authorization: Members only see the catalogue after signing in; only a tool's owner can edit it or decide on its loans; borrowers only see their own requests.
architecture.deployment: One Node.js process behind the host's HTTPS proxy, with the SQLite file on a persistent volume. Deployment is done by a person following RELEASE_PLAN.md.

screens.name: Sign in and sign up
screens.purpose: Join with an invitation code or sign in.

screens.name: Tool details
screens.purpose: See a tool and request it for dates.

screens.name: My loans
screens.purpose: Borrowed and lent loans, with approve, decline and returned actions.

screens.name: My tools
screens.purpose: List, edit and withdraw my tools.

ux.navigation: A top bar with Catalogue, My loans, My tools and Sign out; on phones it wraps onto two lines.

journeys.name: Borrow a tool
steps: See the request under My loans

journeys.name: Lend a tool
steps: List a tool under My tools
See a request under My loans
Mark it returned when it comes back

ux.responsive: Single-column layout below 640 px; forms use full-width inputs; no horizontal scrolling at 360 px.
accessibility: Every input has a visible label
All actions reachable by keyboard with a visible focus outline

entities.name: Member
entities.accessControl: A member reads and changes only their own account; other members see only the name.
entities.retention: Deleted on request together with their tools; loans keep an anonymised placeholder.

entities.name: Tool
entities.description: A tool a member is willing to lend.
entities.accessControl: Signed-in members read; only the owner changes or withdraws.
entities.retention: Kept while the owner is a member; withdrawn tools are hidden but kept for loan history.

entities.name: Loan
entities.description: A request to borrow a tool for dates, and its outcome.

fields.name: toolId
fields.validation: existing Tool not owned by the borrower

fields.name: startDate
fields.validation: not in the past when requested

entities.accessControl: Visible to the borrower and the tool's owner only; only the owner changes the status.
entities.retention: Kept for 2 years for history, then deleted.

integration: Each route with an in-memory SQLite database: sign-up, listing, search, request, approve, decline, return
browser: Manual check on a 360 px wide phone and a desktop browser before release
security: Requests without a session are redirected to sign-in
A member cannot change another member's tool or loan
Forms without a valid CSRF token are refused
Repeated failed sign-ins are slowed down
e2e: Two members: one lists a drill, the other requests it, the first approves and marks it returned

release.hosting: A small container or virtual server host with HTTPS and a persistent volume for the SQLite file (provider chosen by a person).

environmentVariables.name: INVITE_CODE
environmentVariables.purpose: Invitation code required to sign up

release.domains: Optional custom domain configured by a person at the host; the host's default subdomain works for the pilot.
release.migrations: Numbered SQL migration scripts run at start-up inside a transaction; a backup is taken before deploying a new version.
release.backups: Daily copy of the SQLite file to separate storage, kept for 14 days (set up by a person at the host).
release.monitoring: The host's uptime check on /health and its process logs.
legal: A short privacy notice explaining what personal data is stored and how to be deleted (wording to be checked by a person; not legal advice)
publication: Share the sign-up link and invitation code in the neighbourhood chat group

commands.name: test
commands.description: Runs the test suite with Node's test runner

commands.name: build
commands.description: Runs the package.json build script (syntax check of all modules)

tasks.title: Project skeleton and health check
tasks.scope: Create package.json (type module, Node >= 22) with a 'build' script that checks every module (node --check), the folder layout src/ and test/, an HTTP server with a /health route reading PORT, and a README section on running it.
acceptanceCriteria: node --test passes with a test that starts the server and gets 200 from /health
node --run build succeeds
evidence: Passing test output for the health test

tasks.title: Database and migrations
tasks.scope: Open the SQLite database at DATABASE_PATH with node:sqlite, add a migration runner with numbered SQL scripts, and create the member, tool and loan tables with the constraints from DATA_MODEL.md.
acceptanceCriteria: Migrations run once and are recorded
Tables enforce required fields and foreign keys
Tests use an in-memory database
evidence: Test output showing migrations applied to an empty database

tasks.title: Member sign-up, sign-in and sessions
tasks.scope: Sign-up with invitation code (INVITE_CODE), scrypt password hashing, sign-in and sign-out, server-side sessions with a signed cookie (SESSION_SECRET), and the sign-in/sign-up page.
acceptanceCriteria: Sign-up without the invitation code is refused
Wrong passwords are refused
Signed-out visitors are redirected to sign-in
Passwords are stored only as scrypt hashes
evidence: Tests for sign-up, sign-in, sign-out and refused attempts

tasks.title: List, edit and withdraw tools
tasks.scope: My tools page where a member lists a tool (name, description, category), edits it and withdraws it; only the owner may change a tool.
acceptanceCriteria: A listed tool is stored with its owner
Another member's edit attempt gets 403
Withdrawn tools stay in the database but are marked withdrawn
evidence: Tests for create, edit, withdraw and the 403 case

tasks.title: Catalogue, search and tool details
tasks.scope: Catalogue page listing available tools with search by name and filter by category, and a tool details page.
acceptanceCriteria: Search matches part of a tool name, case-insensitive
Category filter works
Withdrawn tools are never listed
evidence: Tests for search, filter and hidden withdrawn tools

tasks.title: Loan requests
tasks.scope: Request form on the tool details page with start and end dates; validation of dates, own tools and overlapping approved loans.
acceptanceCriteria: Past start dates and end dates before start are refused
Requesting one's own tool is refused
A request overlapping an approved loan is refused
evidence: Tests for each refusal rule and a valid request

tasks.title: Decide on loans and My loans page
tasks.scope: My loans page with borrowed and lent sections, overdue highlighting, and approve, decline and mark-returned actions for the lender.
acceptanceCriteria: Only the tool owner can approve, decline or mark returned
Returned tools are available again
Overdue loans are marked
evidence: Tests for each action, the permission check and overdue marking

tasks.title: Responsive and accessible pages
tasks.scope: Shared layout and stylesheet: navigation bar, single-column layout below 640 px, labels, focus outlines, contrast and status messages on every page.
acceptanceCriteria: Every form input has a label element
No fixed widths above 360 px
Status messages use role=status
evidence: Markup tests for labels and roles
Screenshot or notes from a 360 px check in the review

tasks.title: Security hardening
tasks.scope: CSRF tokens on every form, security headers (CSP, frame denial, nosniff), slowing repeated failed sign-ins, and cookie flags for production.
acceptanceCriteria: Forms without a valid CSRF token get 403
Responses carry the security headers
The sixth failed sign-in within 10 minutes is delayed

tasks.title: End-to-end borrowing test
tasks.scope: One test that runs the server with a temporary database and plays the borrow journey with two members through HTTP requests.
acceptanceCriteria: The full journey passes: list, search, request, approve, return
The test cleans up its temporary database

tasks.title: Release preparation
tasks.scope: Write DEPLOY.md (host requirements, environment variables, backups, migrations, privacy notice draft) and .env.example with variable names only. Nothing is deployed.
acceptanceCriteria: .env.example lists every variable from RELEASE_PLAN.md without values
DEPLOY.md covers start-up, migrations, backups and monitoring
evidence: The documents in the review diff

statements.statement: The residents' chat group gets about 10 tool requests per week.
Hosting a small Node.js app with SQLite fits in the 10 USD monthly budget.
node:sqlite is available without flags in current Node.js 22 and 24 releases.
Server-rendered pages without a client framework are enough for this MVP.
